display.purpose: The screen title only, one per route.

body.purpose: Notes, explanations and empty-state teaching copy, at most 70ch.

data.purpose: Scores, counts, call budgets, distances and dates, in tabular figures.

label.purpose: Station names, column headers, buttons and bullets, in capitals at a fixed size.

components.css: .ds-route-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 24px 1fr auto auto; align-items: center; gap: 16px; height: 52px; padding: 0 16px; color: #F2F0EA; background: #0B1230; border-bottom: 1px solid #2B3769; font-family: 'Fira Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-route-row:hover { background: #131C45; } .ds-route-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F2F0EA; outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-route-line { position: relative; display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100%; } .ds-route-line::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: 11px; width: 2px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(#F2F0EA 0 6px, transparent 6px 10px); } .ds-route-suspended { position: relative; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 2px solid #F2F0EA; background: #0B1230; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-route-grid { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-width: 0; } .ds-route-name { font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-route-meta { color: #A9B1CB; font-size: 0.8125rem; } .ds-route-score { color: #A9B1CB; font-family: 'Fira Sans Condensed', 'Fira Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-sources { display: inline-flex; gap: 4px; } .ds-bullet { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 18px; height: 18px; border: 1px solid #F2F0EA; border-radius: 9999px; color: #F2F0EA; text-decoration: none; font-family: 'Fira Sans Condensed', 'Fira Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Strip Map
components.description: A lead's route across both lines: past stations solid, current ringed, ahead dimmed, the grant interchange first.
components.css: .ds-strip { margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: #0B1230; } .ds-strip svg { width: 100%; max-width: 480px; display: block; } .ds-strip path { fill: none; stroke-width: 4; stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-linecap: round; } .ds-strip-out { stroke: #3D74FF; } .ds-strip-ahead { stroke: #0B1230; stroke-width: 2; stroke-dasharray: 6 4; } .ds-strip-grant { stroke: #22B14C; } .ds-strip-tick { fill: #0B1230; stroke: #F2F0EA; stroke-width: 3; } .ds-strip-interchange { fill: #0B1230; stroke: #F2F0EA; stroke-width: 3; } .ds-strip-dim { fill: #A9B1CB; } .ds-strip text { fill: #A9B1CB; font-family: 'Fira Sans Condensed', 'Fira Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 9px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-anchor: middle; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-strip-out { stroke-dasharray: 288; stroke-dashoffset: 288; animation: ds-trace 220ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) forwards; } @keyframes ds-trace { to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } } }

narrative.overview:
LeadForge is drawn as a transit system. The outreach pipeline is a line, the NOF grant pipeline is a second line, every stage is a station, and a business sitting on a City corridor meets both lines at an interchange where the grant line leads. The grammar is the metropolitan rail diagram fired in enamel: disciplined lines that bend only at 45 and 90 degrees, porcelain station ticks, one ink per meaning, and labels set at a fixed size so the network reads the same everywhere. It is borrowed grammar, not borrowed identity: the marks, names and colors are LeadForge's own.

The diagram's honesty is the point. A transit map distinguishes service that runs from service that is planned or suspended, and LeadForge uses exactly that vocabulary for evidence: a version-1 score, a feature that does not run yet and a value nobody measured are drawn as planned or suspended track, dashed or hollow and named in words, never as a solid mark or a zero. Every fact carries lettered source bullets the way a station lists the lines that serve it. Density is welcome; this is an operator's tool, and the ranking is a long table read at a desk.

Two grounds carry one world. Midnight enamel is the native ground; porcelain tile is the daylight ground for long desk sessions. The line inks are shared and tuned per ground so every pairing holds WCAG 2.2 AA. Confirmed rejections: the generic SaaS admin template (stat tiles over pastel kanban columns), and confidence the data has not earned (bold numbers and clean charts that hide what is unmeasured).
keyCharacteristics: Pipelines are lines, stages are stations, grant-first is an interchange.
Planned and suspended marks stand for anything preliminary, unmeasured or not running.
One ink per meaning; one scarlet action plate per screen.
Lettered source bullets (L, G, O) on every fact.
Condensed station labels over tabular data, one type family throughout.
Flat enamel: depth from tone and seams, never from decoration.

rules.name: The Line Owns Its Ink Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is outreach, green is grant, amber is discovery. A line ink never decorates, never marks a generic state, and never appears on a surface that is not about its line.

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: A screen has at most one scarlet filled action. Everything else is a secondary button, a link, or a transfer control.

rules.name: The Never Color Alone Rule
rules.body: Every state a color marks is also marked by shape, pattern or words: line bullets carry letters, planned track is dashed, suspended stations are hollow.

rules.name: The Fixed Label Rule
rules.body: Station and column labels keep one size everywhere; hierarchy comes from the line and its position, never from enlarging a label.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can sit in a column sets in tabular figures, on screen and in tables alike.

rules.name: The Flat Enamel Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat. A shadow appears only on something that floats above the page, and a region is never a card inside a card.

rules.name: The 45/90 Rule
rules.body: No drawn line bends at any other angle, and no line is drawn freehand.

rules.name: The Planned Track Rule
rules.body: A version-1 score, a value never measured and a feature that does not run yet are drawn dashed or hollow and named in words. None of them ever renders as a solid mark or a zero.

dos: Do draw every pipeline as a line and every stage as a station, with transfers as explicit controls.
Do mark unmeasured, preliminary and not-running things as planned or suspended track, in words.
Do put source bullets on every fact, in L, G, O order.
Do keep one scarlet plate per screen, and use the line inks only for their own line.
Do set every number in tabular figures and every station label at its fixed size.
Do check every new pairing at 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for lines and control edges, on both grounds.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces: selection, caret, focus ring, scrollbars and underline offset.
donts: Don't build the generic SaaS admin template: stat tiles over pastel kanban columns, or big-number KPI cards with small labels.
Don't show confidence the data has not earned: no solid mark, zero or default score where a measurement is missing or preliminary.
Don't reproduce any transit agency's own marks, line names or brand colors; the grammar is borrowed, the identity is LeadForge's.
Don't add glow, gradient text, glass, or nested cards.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't make dragging the only way to move a card between stations.
Don't use Unicode glyphs or emoji as icons; icons are one drawn set in one stroke weight.
Don't render synthetic businesses or placeholder data where real records belong; an empty state teaches instead.
